An orthogonal trajectory of a family of curves is a curve that intersects each curve of the family at right angles, or orthogonally (Figure 9.11). For instance, each straight line through the origin is an orthogonal trajectory of the family of circles x2 + y2 = a2, cen- tered at the origin (Figure 9.12). Such mutually orthogonal systems of curves are of particu- lar importance in physical problems related to electrical potential, where the curves in one family correspond to strength of an electric field and those in the other family correspond to constant electric potential. They also occur in hydrodynamics and heat-flow problems.
